Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mia Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, digital transformation, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Jordan to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $14.2 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year on a reported basis and 6.8% on an organic constant-currency basis. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the global CPG industry average of around 4% as tracked by NielsenIQ. Gross margin was 48.7%, expanding 240 basis points year-over-year, driven by supply chain productivity savings, pricing discipline, and favorable mix shifts. Operating income was $2.8 billion, up 11.2%, with operating margin at 19.8%, up 120 basis points. Diluted earnings per share were $1.42, up 14% year-over-year. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me walk you through the details. Volume/mix contributed a modest 1.2%, reflecting disciplined pricing actions amid a 3-4% U.S. inflation backdrop, while pricing alone drove 5.6%. Our average unit retail rose 4.1%, fueled by premiumization in high-margin categories like plant-based snacks and functional beverages, including our expanded lineup of protein-fortified bars under the NutriCore brand, which saw 15% household penetration growth.

Breaking it down by segment: Food & Beverage, our largest at 52% of revenues, grew 7.1% organically to $7.4 billion. Savory snacks and hydration products were standouts, with our Quest-like protein chips gaining 2.2 share points in North America per IRI data, and RTD coffee up 12% in Europe amid the at-home consumption trend. Health & Wellness, 28% of the portfolio, delivered 9.4% organic growth to $4.0 billion, propelled by probiotics and immunity boosters that captured 18% market share in the $15 billion global gut health category, benefiting from post-pandemic wellness tailwinds. Household & Personal Care grew 3.9% organically to $2.8 billion, with our eco-friendly GreenWave cleaning pods driving 22% volume uplift in EMEA as sustainability claims resonate with Gen Z shoppers.

Regionally, North America, 60% of revenues, was up 5.5% organically, with market share gains of 110 basis points in measured channels, though we saw some trade-down pressure in value snacks prompting targeted promotions. Europe grew 8.2% organically, aided by strong performance in premium beauty under GlowEssence skincare. Emerging markets accelerated to 12.4% organically, led by double-digit volume in India and Brazil for affordable hydration packs, with China at 15% growth offsetting slower ASEAN recovery.

Developed markets accounted for 58% of sales, with organic growth at 2.1%, volumes flat, and pricing/mix at 2.1%. North America led at 2.5%, with Zest Snacks up 4% in volume and 110 basis points share gain via Zest Bold Oven-Baked. Europe was softer at 1.5%, with personal care volumes down 1.2% due to downtrading. Emerging markets drove 14.2% organic growth, volumes up 8.5%, led by Asia-Pacific at 16.5% with India beverages +22%, and Latin America at 13.8% with Brazil snacks strong.

On pricing actions, we executed 8.2% average net pricing across the portfolio, driving much of our 5.1% organic sales growth breakdown: pricing +8.2%, offset by -3.1% volume/mix. Price elasticity stabilized at -0.45 to -0.55. Snacks saw +10.1% pricing and +6.8% organic sales with 120 bps share gains versus PepsiCo and Mondelez. Beverages +7.4%, personal care +6.3%. North America +9.1%, Europe +6.2%, emerging +12.4% with volumes up 1.2%. Our 'Price for Value' playbook includes ML promotional optimization cutting ineffective spend by 15%, elasticity modeling on 1.5B POS points, and channel tactics like dynamic e-comm pricing lifting conversion 12%.

Gross margin expansion came from pricing at +310 bps, mix +40 bps, despite commodity headwinds of -110 bps. Input inflation moderated to 4.1%, with cocoa +22%, palm oil +8%, PET +6%, offset by 75% hedging. Pricing realization 92%, with 7.8% list increases. Premium mix from Health & Wellness growing 12%, e-comm at 18% sales. Our Margin Accelerator delivered 80 bps structural uplift.

Supply chain productivity added $450 million in savings from 'Zero-Based Productivity', AI-optimized routing reducing logistics 8% across 250 DCs. These efforts tie into broader efficiencies: procurement $120M YTD via Value Assurance benchmarking P&G/Unilever, palm hedging at $950/MT; logistics $95M via Network Flow 2.0 AI cutting truckload 14%, ocean 9%; manufacturing $70M with OEE +6.5%, inventory turns 7.8x. Total YTD $285M, 55% of 180 bps margin expansion.

Competitively, with ACV growth at 1.2%, private labels at 18.5% in NA, we countered PepsiCo's 22% trade spend hike with NovaPrice 2.0 dynamic algorithms recovering 70 bps share, promo ROI to 3.8x. Innovation countered Beyond Meat with Clean Label launches driving 22% volume. Shelf resets reclaimed 8% space, localized value packs in EM boosted velocity 11%. E-comm bundling lifted DTC 28%.

Promotions at 22% revenue, ROP 3.8x up from 3.2x, sales lift 18%. Precision via PromoOptix AI, reallocated to targeted activations. NA 20% lift, Europe 16%, EM 25%+. Loyalty app 32% repeat, GenAI roadmap for 5x digital ROP.

Balance sheet strong: net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, operating cash flow $3.1B up 22%, FCF $2.4B after $650M capex. Returned $1.8B to shareholders.

For full-year FY2024, raising organic revenue growth to 6.0-6.5%, gross margin +200-250 bps, EPS $5.65-$5.75. Q4 Org CC 5-7%, EPS $1.55-$1.65. Accelerating portfolio shaping with divestitures and DTC beauty acquisition, digital/DTC to 18% sales, sustainability with 30% recycled packaging.

Following my remarks, Mia will provide an update on our marketing and brand performance.

Mia Chen:
Thank you, Jordan. We continue to see strong performance across our key brands. Our marketing investments are driving increased consumer engagement, and we are particularly pleased with the results of our recent LiveBold campaign, which emphasized purpose-driven premiumization and boosted household penetration by double digits in core categories. This aligns with our promotional effectiveness, where we've refined our playbook to achieve higher ROI through data-driven targeting and loyalty integration, countering private label pressures while growing share in premium segments.

After me, Raj will discuss our supply chain initiatives.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Mia. Our focus remains on optimizing our supply chain to enhance efficiency and resilience. We are implementing advanced analytics to improve forecasting and inventory management, delivering substantial productivity savings that have directly supported margin expansion. These include procurement optimizations securing better pricing on key inputs, logistics rerouting via AI platforms reducing costs significantly, and manufacturing gains from Industry 4.0 tech boosting OEE and reducing downtime. Sustainability ties in here, with circular practices like rPET usage cutting costs and enhancing brand appeal.

Finally, Elena will share insights on our innovation pipeline.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Raj. We are excited about the progress we are making on our new product development initiatives. Our pipeline is robust, and we are confident that our innovations will drive future growth. Our recent product, NutriBlast protein-fortified beverage, is showing promising early results, with strong initial distribution and consumer uptake in health and wellness channels, contributing to mix benefits and positioning us ahead in functional categories.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Chris Harlan with JPMorgan.

Chris Harlan:
Can you provide an update on your efforts to reduce packaging waste and the associated cost savings?

Raj Patel:
Thanks, Chris. Reducing packaging waste is a key part of our Planet Positive commitment. We've hit 30% recycled content across packaging, yielding 5% cost savings through circular supply chains, including rPET blends at 35-50% in beverages and cleaners, matching industry leaders. Our GreenWave line and EcoClean products incorporate post-consumer recycled materials, with take-back programs like those with TerraCycle. Piloting blockchain for palm oil traceability preempts regs, and technical reforms like high-oleic oils deliver cost-neutral gains. These efforts contributed $285 million YTD savings, with more from localized manufacturing cutting transport 40% in key markets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Goldman with Goldman Sachs.

Lisa Goldman:
How are you leveraging data analytics to personalize your marketing efforts and improve customer engagement?

Mia Chen:
Great question, Lisa. Data analytics is central to our marketing evolution. Our CB2B platform uses AI for personalization, boosting e-comm conversion 25%, integrated with partnerships like Walmart Connect and Amazon Rufus for shoppable content. PromoOptix and causal modeling from Numerator/IRI data optimize lifts, reducing cannibalization 18%. Loyalty programs like VitaClub, with 18 million members, drive 32% repeat on promos via QR scans and app personalization. Dynamic pricing and geo-fenced tactics in EM like India WhatsApp promos hit 55% redemption, lifting engagement across channels.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Barclays.

Mike Rossi:
What is the expected impact of recent commodity price increases on your gross margins?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Commodities like cocoa up 22-45%, palm oil 8-28%, and energy remain elevated, posing a 110 bps headwind this quarter. We've offset via 75-85% hedging, locked-in futures like corn at $4.85/bushel and palm at $950/MT. Pricing pass-through at 92% realization and productivity savings of $450M more than cover, delivering 240 bps expansion. Q4 inflation at 3.5%, with Supplier Collaboration stabilizing. Emerging market devaluations amplify, but nearshoring and efficiencies mitigate—expect continued 100-150 bps FY expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Dana Patel:
Can you discuss the competitive landscape and any emerging trends that are impacting your market share?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Dana. The landscape is intense with 1.2% ACV growth, private labels at 18.5%, and disruptors in health. Peers like PepsiCo, Mondelez ramped trade 22%, but our NovaPrice AI and deeper TPRs recovered 70 bps, with 3.8x ROI. Innovation counters Beyond/Impossible with Clean Label launches at 85% distro, 22% volume. Shelf battles via Reset 2024 reclaimed 8%, value packs in EM +11% velocity. Trends like polarization favor our 40/40/20 portfolio, health/sustainability where we're certified on 70%, and channel shifts with DTC +28%. We're gaining 50 bps FY share, outpacing via defend/attack/partner playbook.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Alex for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your thoughtful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to updating you next quarter.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
